**Name of the Surah**

• It is called Ṣād, because it opens with this letter standing alone at its beginning, as a challenge and a demonstration of the Qur'an's inimitability (iʿjāz).

**Some of the Surah's Aims**

• To highlight the status of the Qur'an, and to rebuke the polytheists for their denial and obstinacy towards the Messenger (ﷺ). It also addresses their disbelief and astonishment that revelation should descend upon such a man, responds to their doubt about the Messenger's (ﷺ) humanity and their denial of the Oneness of Divinity (tawḥīd al-ulūhiyyah), and sets forth as an example for those arrogant Quraysh disbelievers the peoples before them who were stubborn and defiant.

• To narrate the stories of some of the Prophets, as consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) for what he suffered from his people, so that he might follow the Prophets before him, and to show God's mercy towards His messengers through the care, favour and blessings He bestowed upon them. All of this is a response to the amazement of the disbelievers that God chose Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger from among them.

• To speak of some of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, the reward of the faithful who are God-conscious, and the fate of their opposites, the tyrants and wrongdoers.

• To mention the story of Adam and Iblīs's refusal to prostrate to him, indicating that what the polytheists did in their arrogance and their refusal to accept that revelation should descend upon the Messenger (ﷺ) instead of them, is nothing but the whispering of Iblīs, and that what they did is an imitation of the qualities with which he adorned them.

David said: "He has certainly wronged you by asking to add your ewe to his ewes. Indeed, many partners wrong one another, one oppressing the other by taking his right and not being fair to himself, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; and they are few." And David realized that We had tested him with this dispute, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down in prostration, drawing near to Allah, and turned back to Him in repentance.
So We forgave him that, made him among those brought near to Us, and prepared for him a good final destination in the Hereafter.

O David! We have made you a successor (khalifah) on the earth and given you dominion in it. So judge between the people with justice and equity, and do not follow your whims in judgments, lest it lead you astray from the religion of God and His law. Indeed, those who stray from the path of God will have a painful punishment in the Fire, because of their heedlessness of the Day of Recompense and Reckoning. In this is an admonition to rulers that they should judge by the truth sent down from God, may He be blessed and exalted, and not deviate from it, lest they stray from His path.

Iblis said: "By Your might, O Lord, and by Your majesty, I will surely mislead all of the children of Adam, except those among them whom You have made sincere (purified) for Your worship, and whom You have protected from my misguidance. So You have not given me any authority over them."

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists of your people: "I do not ask you for any wage or reward for my calling you and guiding you, nor do I claim a matter that is not mine. Rather, I follow only what is revealed to me, and I do not burden myself with conjecture and fabrication."
This Qur'an is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, to jinn and humankind, through which they remember what benefits them in the interests of their religion and their worldly life.

And you will surely come to know the truth of this Qur'an and its veracity, O polytheists, when Islam prevails and people enter it in multitudes, and likewise when punishment befalls you and the means (of escape) are cut off from you.
